title: FDA's Rare Disease Evidence Principles and Evidentiary Flexibility for Ultra-Rare Disease Programs
summary: How FDA's RDEP process works, plus single-trial approvals, external controls, surrogate endpoints and other evidence flexibility for rare disease programs.
body_markdown:
## FDA's Rare Disease Evidence Principles (RDEP) and evidentiary flexibility for small-population and ultra-rare disease programs


FDA has not created a lower approval standard for rare diseases. Its rare disease guidance states that the statutory effectiveness requirement is the same for rare and common diseases, and that the Orphan Drug Act does not create a different approval standard for orphan drugs[118](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=118)[276](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=276) . What FDA has done is define, with growing specificity, how sponsors can meet the substantial evidence standard when patient numbers make conventional development programs impractical. The Rare Disease Evidence Principles (RDEP), announced in September 2025, is the most targeted of these mechanisms. It sits within a wider set of guidance, pilot programs and review practices covering single-trial approvals, natural history and external controls, surrogate endpoints, innovative trial designs and individualized therapies.


### What RDEP is


FDA announced RDEP on September 3, 2025, as a review process intended to give sponsors clearer direction on how to demonstrate substantial evidence of effectiveness for therapies that target rare diseases with very small patient populations, significant unmet need and a known genetic defect[19](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles) . CDER and CBER developed and implement the process jointly[23](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles)[24](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles) .


FDA's stated rationale is that in very small rare disease populations, running multiple traditional clinical trials can be difficult or impossible while still meeting the statutory evidence standard. RDEP is meant to offer a rigorous, viable alternative and more predictability about the supportive evidence FDA will consider[19](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles)[25](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles) . FDA also described traditional designs, including placebo-controlled studies, as especially difficult in very small populations[134](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-launches-program-for-rare-diseases-targeting.html)[135](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-launches-program-for-rare-diseases-targeting.html)[136](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-launches-program-for-rare-diseases-targeting.html) .


#### Eligibility criteria


Criterion What FDA requires


Mechanism The investigational therapy must specifically address the underlying genetic defect[20](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles)


Population size The rare disease population or subpopulation is generally fewer than 1,000 U.S. patients[20](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles)


Disease course Patients face rapid functional deterioration leading to disability or death[20](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles)


Unmet need No adequate alternative therapy exists[20](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles)


Rare cancers Sponsors should first consult the Oncology Center of Excellence or the relevant review division on whether RDEP applies[22](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles)


#### Evidence standard under RDEP


Under RDEP, approval may be based on one adequate and well-controlled study plus robust confirmatory evidence. FDA was explicit that this does not mean approval on a single trial alone[21](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles) . Examples of confirmatory evidence FDA cited include:


- mechanistic or biomarker evidence, including effects on the disease's direct pathophysiology[21](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles)[136](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-launches-program-for-rare-diseases-targeting.html)
- data from relevant nonclinical models[21](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles)[136](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-launches-program-for-rare-diseases-targeting.html)
- clinically significant pharmacodynamic data[21](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles)[136](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-launches-program-for-rare-diseases-targeting.html)
- case reports and expanded access data[21](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles)[136](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-launches-program-for-rare-diseases-targeting.html)
- natural history studies[21](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles)


Products approved through this route may carry additional postmarketing requirements to further establish safety and effectiveness[23](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles)[24](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles) .


#### Process and timing


A sponsor requests RDEP review as part of a formal meeting request, and the request must be made before the pivotal trial begins[22](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles) . Sponsors accepted into the process then meet with the relevant FDA review team to determine which data will substantiate safety and effectiveness, and FDA encourages patient and expert input throughout[22](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles)[137](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-launches-program-for-rare-diseases-targeting.html)[138](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-launches-program-for-rare-diseases-targeting.html) . The announcement did not set a fixed review or approval timeline[123](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-launches-program-for-rare-diseases-targeting.html) .


#### What RDEP does not do


- RDEP is separate from orphan drug designation. Participation neither confers orphan designation nor affects eligibility for it[24](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles)[139](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-launches-program-for-rare-diseases-targeting.html) .
- RDEP does not change the statutory standard. It clarifies how the existing "one adequate and well-controlled investigation plus confirmatory evidence" route applies to a narrowly defined population[21](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles)[134](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-launches-program-for-rare-diseases-targeting.html) .
- Public reporting through late 2026 has not disclosed the number of RDEP requests received, programs accepted, or products approved under the process[123](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-launches-program-for-rare-diseases-targeting.html)[127](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-s-handling-of-rare-disease-therapies-criticize.html) . No CDER MAPP or CBER SOPP describing RDEP procedures has been identified in FDA's published procedure documents; the publicly available procedural detail comes from FDA's announcement[61](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=61) .


FDA positioned RDEP as building on and complementing its earlier Accelerating Rare Disease Cures (ARC) program, the START pilot and the Rare Disease Endpoint Advancement (RDEA) pilot[152](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-launches-program-for-rare-diseases-targeting.html) .


### The legal and policy foundation: one trial plus confirmatory evidence


RDEP applies a principle FDA has articulated for decades. FDA's final guidance *Providing Clinical Evidence of Effectiveness for Human Drug and Biological Products* (May 1998) explains that substantial evidence ordinarily rests on independent substantiation, but that the statute permits FDA to rely on one adequate and well-controlled investigation plus confirmatory evidence. A single favorable study is not automatically sufficient; its design and results must be persuasive, and conflicting studies matter[194](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=194)[195](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=195)[196](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=196)[197](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=197) .


Two later drafts expand on this:


- *Demonstrating Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness With One Adequate and Well-Controlled Clinical Investigation and Confirmatory Evidence* (draft, September 2023) states that FDA assesses the investigation and the confirmatory evidence together, case by case. A highly persuasive investigation may need less confirmatory support; a less persuasive one needs more compelling corroboration. Sponsors should discuss the approach early[174](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=174)[170](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=170) .
- *Demonstrating Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness for Human Drug and Biological Products* (draft, June 24, 2026) lists the factors FDA weighs for a single-trial approach: trial design, conduct, analysis and persuasiveness; the source and strength of corroboration; disease seriousness, unmet need and prevalence; and whether another trial would be ethical and practicable. It generally expects either a highly persuasive trial or strong confirmatory evidence[172](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=172) . For rare diseases, it acknowledges that smaller trials yield less precise estimates and stresses interpretable design (randomization, blinding, appropriate endpoints, covariate adjustment, adequate duration), while allowing scientifically sound flexibility in the source and strength of confirmatory evidence[111](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=111) . It recommends discussing a proposed single-trial approach with FDA before that trial begins, and no later than the end-of-phase 2 meeting[315](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=315)[316](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=316) .


#### Types of confirmatory evidence FDA has described


Source Conditions and caveats


Clinical evidence from a closely related indication Relatedness depends on similarity of pathophysiology, mechanism of action and endpoints[170](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=170)[189](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=189)


Evidence from drugs in the same pharmacological class Mechanisms and effects must be sufficiently similar and consistent[198](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=198)


Mechanistic or pharmacodynamic evidence (clinical or nonclinical) Most useful when disease pathophysiology and the drug's mechanism are well understood, for example correction of a causal gene or enzyme defect; plausible pharmacologic effects do not always predict clinical benefit[111](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=111)[199](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=199)


Natural history evidence Should be distinct from data used as the trial's control; real-world data sources must be assessed for reliability and relevance[186](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=186)


Expanded access outcomes May be considered if highly persuasive, though FDA notes such information is typically too limited or inconsistent[200](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=200)


A RAPS report from April 2026 quoted an FDA official describing a newer default of one well-designed clinical trial when it provides sufficient evidence, noting that single-trial evidence was already used in rare disease development and that the newer approach extends beyond it[162](https://www.raps.org/resource/h-eg-touts-fda-efforts-to-speed-rare-disease-drugs-to-market.html) . FDA's June 2026 draft guidance describes both single-trial and multiple-trial approaches without stating a universal default[172](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=172)[314](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=314) .


### Flexibility in rare disease development guidance


The final guidance *Rare Diseases: Considerations for the Development of Drugs and Biological Products* (December 2023) is the core reference for program design. Its key flexibilities:


- **Trial design.** FDA may consider design flexibility case by case, particularly where natural history is predictable and the treatment has a large effect on an objectively and reliably measured endpoint, while generally recommending a randomized concurrent control[102](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=102) . The guidance describes Bayesian methods, n-of-1 trials, delayed-start and crossover designs, and master protocols, and notes that modified designs can reduce placebo exposure[107](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=107) .
- **Endpoints.** Natural history studies can inform disease course and endpoint selection[119](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=119) . A novel clinical outcome assessment may be needed where existing measures are infeasible, with early FDA discussion recommended[100](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=100) .
- **Safety database.** Exposure expectations developed for chronic drugs in non-life-threatening conditions do not apply to many life-threatening rare diseases, and fewer exposed patients may be acceptable when the intended population is small[122](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=122) .
- **Clinical pharmacology.** The draft *Rare Diseases: Early Drug Development and the Role of Pre-IND Meetings* (October 2018) says FDA can be flexible about which clinical pharmacology studies are essential, whether they are integrated into efficacy and safety trials, and which can be deferred until after approval. It also supports modeling and simulation to inform dosing and trial design[121](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=121)[105](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=105) .


FDA's expedited programs guidance also states that FDA applies flexibility to the particular development challenges of rare diseases[277](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=277) . Disease-specific guidance can make the single-trial expectation explicit: the draft *Mucopolysaccharidosis Type III* guidance states that, given the disease's rarity, one adequate and well-controlled trial showing a clinically meaningful effect plus confirmatory evidence can support approval[265](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=265) .


### Natural history data and external controls


FDA treats natural history as valuable but not as a substitute for a credible comparison. Randomized concurrent controls remain the preferred approach for separating a drug effect from disease progression[102](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=102) .


- The December 2023 rare disease guidance advises sponsors to assess the quality of existing natural history knowledge early and favors prospectively designed, protocol-driven natural history studies[254](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=254) . External or historical controls are usually reserved for well-characterized natural history, predictable mortality or progressive morbidity, and a large, self-evident drug effect[257](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=257)[258](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=258) .
- The draft *Rare Diseases: Natural History Studies for Drug Development* (March 2019) describes natural history studies as useful for planning controlled trials and potentially supplying external control data, and identifies concurrent external data as a stronger design than past patient-level data[255](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=255)[256](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=256) .
- The final *Human Gene Therapy for Rare Diseases* (January 2020) allows a single-arm trial with historical controls when randomization is infeasible, but only if treated and control populations are adequately matched on disease state, demographics, concurrent treatment and other factors[259](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=259)[260](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=260) .
- The draft *Considerations for the Design and Conduct of Externally Controlled Trials for Drug and Biological Products* (February 2023) confirms that an appropriate externally controlled trial can serve as an adequate and well-controlled investigation[261](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=261)[232](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=232) . It warns that unmeasured confounding and lack of blinding cannot be eliminated, and recommends prespecifying the external control and analysis before the trial rather than selecting a comparator after seeing single-arm results[262](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=262)[263](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=263)[233](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=233)[235](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=235) . Historical comparisons are especially vulnerable to changes in diagnosis and standard of care[238](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=238)[239](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=239)[264](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=264) .


### Accelerated approval and surrogate endpoints


Accelerated approval allows reliance on a surrogate or intermediate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit for serious conditions where a drug offers a meaningful advantage over available therapy[363](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=363)[364](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=364)[365](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=365) . For rare diseases, sponsors may consider surrogate endpoints when a clinical endpoint changes too slowly to assess in a trial of reasonable duration, and natural history data, animal models, patient data and early pharmacodynamic data can help support a proposed biomarker[366](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=366)[351](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=351) . The rare disease gene therapy guidance also states that sponsors may consider accelerated approval based on a surrogate endpoint[120](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=120)[367](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=367) .


The draft *Accelerated Approval: Expedited Program for Serious Conditions* (December 2024) adds rare disease-specific nuance. Where trial evidence linking surrogate changes to clinical outcomes is limited, FDA may weigh converging evidence from animal models, epidemiology and clinical data, and in certain circumstances compelling nonclinical evidence may support a rare disease surrogate without clinical data establishing that relationship[347](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=347)[368](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=368)[348](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=348)[369](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=369) . Pharmacologic activity alone is insufficient[347](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=347) . The draft identifies the RDEA pilot as an option for collaborating on novel surrogate or intermediate endpoints[370](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=370) . Confirmatory postapproval studies remain required, and FDA can specify protocol, enrollment and completion milestones by the time of approval[371](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=371)[372](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=372)[373](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=373) .


### Cell and gene therapy in small populations


The draft *Innovative Designs for Clinical Trials of Cellular and Gene Therapy Products in Small Populations* (September 24, 2025) describes several design options[321](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=321)[1](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=1) :


- **Disease progression modeling** of natural history using biomarker trajectories, clinical endpoints and patient heterogeneity, with caveats about variable progression, evolving standard of care and model validation in underrepresented subgroups[321](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=321) .
- **Externally controlled studies** using historical or real-world data, with suitability judged case by case[321](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=321) .
- **Single-arm trials with participants as their own control** , comparing outcomes with a reliably established baseline, while noting that fluctuating disease and regression to the mean can confound interpretation[3](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=3) .
- **Adaptive designs** , including early stopping, sample-size reassessment, enrichment and dose selection followed by confirmation in one study, all requiring rigorous prespecification[323](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=323) .
- **Bayesian designs** that can incorporate external clinical data, including existing control data to augment a concurrent control group[342](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=342) .


On the CMC side, the final *Human Gene Therapy for Neurodegenerative Diseases* (October 2022) advises sponsors whose small early-phase studies may supply effectiveness evidence to establish critical quality attributes and controls early, and to consider multiple small lots to build process experience[222](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=222) . The draft *Leveraging Prior Knowledge in the Development of Human Gene Therapy Products Incorporating Genome Editing* (June 2026) describes scientifically justified reuse of prior CMC, nonclinical and clinical knowledge to reduce new data requirements[223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=223)[224](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=224)[225](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=225) .


### Ultra-rare and individualized therapies


For the smallest populations, FDA has issued guidance aimed at therapies developed for one or a few patients.


**Individualized antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs).** Two 2021 drafts address ASOs for severely debilitating or life-threatening genetic diseases where the targeted variant is generally reported in only one or two patients[26](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=26)[57](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=57) . The nonclinical draft (April 2021) recommends a less extensive first-in-human safety package than for broader-use ASOs, offset by convincing in vitro or in vivo proof of concept, with off-target binding assessment and route-appropriate safety pharmacology[32](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=32)[60](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=60) . FDA cautions that abbreviated testing may miss toxicity and that larger populations or commercialization typically warrant additional studies[41](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=41) . The clinical draft (December 2021) covers IND content, dosing and monitoring, and asks sponsors to document the variant's rarity[26](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=26)[58](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=58)[36](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=36)[59](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=59) .


**Plausible Mechanism Framework.** On February 23, 2026, CDER and CBER issued the draft *Considerations for the use of the Plausible Mechanism Framework to Develop Individualized Therapies that Target Specific Genetic Conditions with Known Biological Cause*[293](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-launches-framework-accelerating-development-individualized-therapies-ultra-rare-diseases)[33](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=33) . It addresses evidence of effectiveness and safety for genome-editing and RNA-based therapies when randomized trials are infeasible and data will come from a limited number of patients[293](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-launches-framework-accelerating-development-individualized-therapies-ultra-rare-diseases)[294](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-launches-framework-accelerating-development-individualized-therapies-ultra-rare-diseases)[33](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=33) . Key elements:


- FDA anticipates that one adequate and well-controlled investigation with confirmatory evidence could establish effectiveness[204](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=204) .
- Where untreated natural history can be reasonably characterized, comparing a patient's post-treatment change with baseline or an estimate of the untreated course may be acceptable, particularly when the effect is rapid, dramatic and unlikely to occur spontaneously[44](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=44)[227](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=227) .
- Sponsors should confirm the diagnosis and show that the targeted variant is causal and rare[40](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=40) .
- FDA described possible single applications and master protocols covering related genome-editing variants[295](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-launches-framework-accelerating-development-individualized-therapies-ultra-rare-diseases)[159](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-proposes-plausible-mechanism-pathway-for-ultra.html)[160](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-proposes-plausible-mechanism-pathway-for-ultra.html) .
- The choice between traditional and accelerated approval, and specific endpoints, is left to discussion with the review division[228](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=228) .


FDA later clarified that it had proposed a framework operating within existing regulatory pathways, not a new pathway[161](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-official-data-quality-is-key-to-plausible-mechanism-framework.html) .


### Engagement programs that support evidence planning


Program Center Key features

Rare Disease Innovation Hub CDER and CBER Cross-center program and single point of external engagement; January 2025 strategic agenda covering regulatory science, center coordination and a centralized contact[291](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-roundup-november-1-2024)[292](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-roundup-january-17-2025)[153](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-unveils-rare-disease-innovation-hub-plans-pub.html)[154](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-unveils-rare-disease-innovation-hub-plans-pub.html)

### Flexibility in recent approvals


Recent FDA approval announcements show how these principles are being applied in specific products:


- **Waskyra** (Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome gene therapy, December 2025): FDA cited appropriate use of expanded access data and flexibility in trial design, mechanism of action and manufacturing review[296](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-gene-therapy-treatment-wiskott-aldrich-syndrome)[297](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-gene-therapy-treatment-wiskott-aldrich-syndrome) .
- **Avlayah** (neurologic manifestations of Hunter syndrome, March 2026): accelerated approval based on a surrogate endpoint reasonably likely to predict benefit, with a clinical benefit trial underway[298](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-gene-therapy-treatment-wiskott-aldrich-syndrome)[299](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-drug-treat-neurologic-manifestations-hunter-syndrome) .
- **Kresladi** (severe leukocyte adhesion deficiency type I gene therapy, March 2026): evidence from one open-label, single-arm study, with accelerated approval on a surrogate endpoint subject to confirmatory studies. FDA said it considers small trial populations and all available sources of evidence in rare diseases[300](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-gene-therapy-severe-leukocyte-adhesion-deficiency-type-i)[301](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-gene-therapy-severe-leukocyte-adhesion-deficiency-type-i)[302](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-gene-therapy-severe-leukocyte-adhesion-deficiency-type-i) .
- **Otarmeni** (genetic hearing loss gene therapy, April 2026): evidence from a single ongoing single-arm trial supported by confirmatory mechanistic nonclinical data and sustained protein expression, approved under the National Priority Voucher program[345](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-ever-gene-therapy-treatment-genetic-hearing-loss-under-national-priority-voucher)[346](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-ever-gene-therapy-treatment-genetic-hearing-loss-under-national-priority-voucher) .


These announcements are product-specific examples and do not identify any of these products as RDEP approvals.


### Open questions and stakeholder concerns


Stakeholders have welcomed RDEP but questioned consistency in rare disease reviews. At a Senate hearing reported on February 26, 2026, an EveryLife Foundation representative said FDA decisions on rare disease applications appeared inconsistent with its stated commitment to flexibility. She cited hesitation over surrogate endpoints, natural history studies, external controls and real-world evidence, and reported at least 23 complete response letters for rare disease therapies submitted under accelerated approval since the start of 2025[127](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-s-handling-of-rare-disease-therapies-criticize.html)[140](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-s-handling-of-rare-disease-therapies-criticize.html) . These criticisms concerned FDA's broader rare disease reviews, not RDEP decisions[140](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-s-handling-of-rare-disease-therapies-criticize.html) .


Several practical questions remain open in the public record: how many programs have entered RDEP, how the process will interact with the Plausible Mechanism Framework and the Rare Disease Framework Initiative, and whether the October 2026 initiative will produce changes to evidentiary standards, endpoints, statistics, trial design or postapproval requirements[123](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-launches-program-for-rare-diseases-targeting.html)[163](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-launches-rare-disease-framework-initiative.html)[164](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-launches-rare-disease-framework-initiative.html)[165](https://www.raps.org/resource/fda-launches-rare-disease-framework-initiative.html) .


### Practical implications for sponsors


- **Assess RDEP eligibility before the pivotal trial.** The request window closes once the pivotal study starts, and it is made through a formal meeting request[22](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles) .
- **Plan confirmatory evidence deliberately.** Under both RDEP and FDA's general single-trial guidance, the persuasiveness of the trial and the strength of corroborating mechanistic, pharmacodynamic, nonclinical, natural history or expanded access data are weighed together[21](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-advances-rare-disease-drug-development-new-evidence-principles)[172](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=172)[174](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=174) .
- **Invest early in natural history.** Prospective, protocol-driven natural history data support endpoint selection, surrogate justification and any external control[254](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=254)[119](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=119)[366](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=366) .
- **Prespecify any external control and analysis.** FDA expects these choices to be fixed before results are known[235](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=235) .
- **Use the engagement programs.** START, RDEA and the Rare Disease Innovation Hub provide additional channels for design and endpoint discussions[391](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-launches-pilot-program-help-further-accelerate-development-rare-disease-therapies)[370](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=370)[291](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-roundup-november-1-2024) .
- **Treat flexibility as case-specific.** FDA's guidance consistently frames these approaches as case-by-case, with randomized concurrent controls still preferred where feasible[102](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=102)[111](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fdas-rare-disease-evidence-principles-rdep?showSourceNumber=111) .
